title: Weaver MoT Block
body:
# Description

Adds the **Weaver** core dual-pathway attention block (`WeaverDualAttention`), per-tower feed-forward block (`WeaverMLP`), and dual-pathway Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) decoder layer (`WeaverMoTDecoderLayer`) to MaxText.

### Context & Motivation
Weaver uses a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture with two parallel transformer towers that maintain independent weights (projections, QK norms, pre/post RMSNorms, and MLPs) while sharing a single fused attention step:
- **Understanding pathway (`und`)**: processes text/prompt tokens using sample-isolated causal self-attention.
- **Generation pathway (`gen`)**: processes continuous multimodal/latent tokens using sample-isolated full bidirectional attention that also cross-attends to the understanding stream's keys and values.

Previously, MaxText lacked native support for dual-pathway packed sequence routing, asymmetric cross-pathway QK normalization (`k_norm_und_for_gen`), and the dual-tower MoT decoder block required to run Weaver (`weaver-mini` and `weaver-max`) models.

### Implementation Details
1. **Self-Contained Weaver Model Package (`src/maxtext/models/weaver/weaver.py`, `src/maxtext/models/weaver/__init__.py`)**:
   - `WeaverConfig`: Typed dataclass configuration for Weaver Mixture-of-Transformers blocks, including configurable logical sharding `kernel_axes`.
   - `WeaverPackingMetadata` & `build_weaver_packing_metadata`: constructs cumulative sample boundary offsets (`causal_q_offsets`, `full_q_offsets`, `sample_kv_offsets`) and stream scatter/gather index maps (`packed_und_token_indexes`, `packed_gen_token_indexes`).
   - `unpack_streams` & `reinterleave_streams`: splits interleaved packed token sequences into understanding/generation streams and merges outputs back into global packed sequence order (with optional TPU SparseCore ragged ops).
   - `compute_3d_mrope_cos_sin` & `apply_rotary_pos_emb`: implements 3D Multimodal Rotary Position Embeddings (3D M-RoPE) across temporal, height, and width sections.
   - `causal_understanding_attention` & `full_generative_attention`: supports `dot_product`, `flash`, and `splash` attention backends with strict cross-sample isolation masks (`build_causal_understanding_mask`, `build_full_generative_mask`, and Tokamax Splash mask compilation via `compile_weaver_splash_mask`).
   - `WeaverDualAttention` (`WeaverAttention`): Pure `flax.nnx` module (`nnx.Linear`, `nnx.RMSNorm`) encapsulating independent understanding and generation projections (`q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`/`o_proj` and `*_gen`), independent QK RMSNorms, and optional cross-pathway `k_norm_und_for_gen`.
   - `WeaverMLP`: per-tower feed-forward block supporting both gated SwiGLU (`hidden_act="silu"`, `weaver-mini`) and ungated squared-ReLU (`hidden_act="relu2"`, `weaver-max`).
   - `WeaverMoTDecoderLayer`: composes `WeaverDualAttention` with independent understanding and generation towers:
     - Understanding pathway: `input_layernorm`, `to_q`, `to_k`, `to_v`, `to_out`, `norm_q`, `norm_k`, `post_attention_layernorm`, `mlp`.
     - Generation pathway: `input_layernorm_moe_gen`, `add_q_proj`, `add_k_proj`, `add_v_proj`, `to_add_out`, `norm_added_q`, `norm_added_k`, `post_attention_layernorm_moe_gen`, `mlp_moe_gen`.
   - Exposes canonical parameter names (`to_q`, `add_q_proj`, `to_add_out`, `norm_added_q`, etc.) as zero-copy property aliases onto `self_attn` so checkpoint loaders and parity tests can address either naming convention without duplicating parameters in the NNX graph.

   - Sample-isolation and causality invariance tests for both Kernel 1 (`causal_understanding_attention`) and Kernel 2 (`full_generative_attention`).
   - 3D M-RoPE shape and norm-preservation checks.
   - `jax.jit` compilation, `nnx.grad` backprop flow, and `dot_product` / `flash` / `splash` kernel parity.
   - **Attention Golden Parity (`WeaverDualAttentionGoldenParityTest`)**: verifies numerical parity against reference golden activations (`gs://maxtext-test-assets/weaver_attention_golden_data.npz`) across MHA, GQA, `weaver-max` asymmetric QK-norm, and no-RoPE configurations:

title: Expose enable_continuous_profiling CLI flag in MaxText
body: # Description Expose the `enable_continuous_profiling` CLI configuration flag in MaxText to support saving trace profiles larger than 2GB as `.xplane.riegeli`. ### Context & Solution: When profiling large model workloads or multi-step training runs, monolithic `.xplane.pb` trace files can exceed Protocol Buffer's 2GB wire format limit, leading to serialization and file upload failures. title: [MaxText] Add spatial minor [k, n, g] TGMM kernel
body:
# Description

Port of cl/979649927.

Some consumers of `tgmm_v2` want its output in the spatial minor layout `[k, n, g]`, with the group axis on lanes. Getting there from `tgmm_v2` needs a relayout copy that materializes a second full size output in HBM.

This PR adds `tgmm_spatial_minor_v2`, a Pallas kernel that writes `[k, n, g]` directly. Each output tile is written to HBM once. A per group matmul fills a VMEM stage, and a register transpose built on native XLU transposes produces the output layout on chip. `tgmm_gnk_v2` dispatches on the requested layout and falls back to `tgmm_v2` plus a transpose. `tgmm_v2` gains input validation for operand ranks, `group_offset` forms and unaligned `m`.

On Ghostfish at `m=4096, k=7168, n=2048`, bf16:

| g | kernel | `tgmm_v2` + copy | peak HBM, kernel vs copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 8.75 ms | 6.16 ms | 3.83 GB vs 7.59 GB |
| 16 | 3.26 ms | 2.92 ms | 3.83 GB vs 4.30 GB |

The kernel trades latency for half the peak HBM at `g=128`.
No existing caller changes.

# Tests

- Unit tests in `tests/unit/pallas_mosaic_tpu_v2_kernel_test.py` covering:
  - Numerical correctness tests against NumPy reference
  - Equivalence against existing `tgmm_v2` baseline
  - Dynamic `group_offset` slicing and window shifting
  - Input validation (operand ranks, mismatched shapes, layout permutations)
  - Dtype coverage (bf16/f32 inputs/outputs and accumulation)
  - Layout dispatch and HLO entry computation verification

title: DeepSeek V4 MTP Support
body:
# Description

Adds Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) support for DeepSeek V4, covering both the model layers and checkpoint conversion.

DeepSeek V4 carries a 4D residual stream `[batch, seq, mhc_expansion_rate, emb]` through the decoder (Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections), whereas V3 is plain 3D. Enabling MTP for V4 therefore means handling two orthogonal concerns at the prediction head:

- **Normalization**, which was already solved by the `normalize_y` flag added for V3 MTP in "Add separate final normalization for Multi-Token Prediction in DeepSeek models". This change reuses that mechanism rather than introducing a parallel one.
- **Collapsing the mHC streams**, which is V4-specific and is introduced here as a `reduce_mhc` flag on `apply_output_head`.

`NNXDecoder.__call__` now leaves the hidden state expanded and defers the collapse to `apply_output_head`, so the MTP block receives the full 4D state. Each MTP depth collapses it with its own learned hyper-connection head, applies its dedicated final norm, and then projects to logits with both normalization and reduction disabled. The unnormalized 4D state is what carries to the next depth:

```
NNXDecoder.__call__  ->  hidden_state = y          (stays 4D)
  main logits:  apply_output_head(hidden_state)     # reduce_mhc=True -> hc_head, then decoder_norm
  mtp_block(main_hidden_state=hidden_state)         # receives the full 4D state
      per depth k:  MTP layer (4D in -> 4D out)
                 -> mtp_layer.hc_head(...)          # 4D -> 3D, per-depth learned collapse
                 -> mtp_layer.final_norm(...)       # dedicated MTP RMSNorm
                 -> apply_output_head(..., normalize_y=False, reduce_mhc=False)
```

`reduce_mhc` defaults to `True`, which preserves existing behaviour for every current caller of `apply_output_head` (main logits, vocab tiling, and the vLLM adapter).

Two V4-specific details worth a reviewer's attention:

- `MultiTokenPredictionLayer` constructs a `DeepSeek4DecoderLayer` directly rather than using `transformer_layer_module`. With `scan_layers=True`, `get_decoder_layers()` returns a `DeepSeek4ScannableBlock` (a bundled HCA + CSA pair), which is not a single layer and cannot serve as an MTP layer.
- The per-depth `hc_head` is deliberately left unprefixed, unlike the other MTP submodules which are renamed to `mtp_{k}_*`, so that it matches the checkpoint key layout.

This also removes the config validation error that previously rejected `DecoderBlockType.DEEPSEEK4` in combination with MTP layers.

# Tests

**Unit tests**

- `tests/unit/param_mapping_test.py` — 35 passed. Adds three DeepSeek V4 MTP cases: the keys the MTP block contributes, that they disappear when `mtp_num_layers=0`, and a split/rejoin round-trip for the fused projection kernel.
- `tests/unit/multi_token_prediction_test.py` and `tests/unit/flop_calculation_test.py` — 84 passed, 9 skipped (skips unrelated to this change).

**Checkpoint conversion**

The MaxText-side keys generated for the MTP block were diffed against the `mtp_block` keys actually present in a converted DeepSeek V4 MTP checkpoint: an exact 45/45 match, no missing and no extra keys, for both `scan_layers=True` and `scan_layers=False`. That also confirms the MTP transformer layer carries a MoE gate bias but neither a compressor nor a hash-routing table, consistent with it being built with `compress_ratio=0` and `is_hash_routing=False`.

**End-to-end**

DeepSeek V4 284B on v5p-128 (64 devices), C4, `mtp_num_layers=1`, `mtp_eval_target_module=1`, `max_target_length=2048`, bf16, evaluating after each of 3 steps:

| Step | `mtp_acceptance_rate` | eval loss | perplexity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 79.09% | 2.234 | 9.338 |
| 1 | 79.12% | 2.234 | 9.338 |
| 2 | 79.13% | 2.234 | 9.337 |

title: [MLPerf] Cherry-pick #5293, #5207, #5355, #5360 from main
body:
# Description

Cherry-picks four commits from `main` into `atwigg/mlperf`, applied in the order they landed on main. Each commit keeps its original author and has a `(cherry picked from commit …)` line.

| Commit on main | Original PR | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| edfd9fcc1 | #5293 | Adds `quantize_router_proj` (default `true`). When `false`, a qwix rule keeps the MoE router (`.*/gate$`) matmul unquantized. Only has an effect when `use_qwix_quantization=True` and `quantization` is set. |
| 341466e6e | #5207 | Adds `quantization="serve_fp8_weight"`, which runs FP8 weights natively (no dequantization) at inference time in `DenseGeneral` (qwix FP8 dot_general), the fused vLLM MoE path, and the gmm_v2 MoE path. Also passes `quant` into the Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 GDN projections. |
| 4d3d1535e | #5355 | Fixes AOT compilation for the ragged kernels (`pltpu.is_tpu_device()` instead of checking `jax.devices()[0].platform`) and passes data sharding into `load_compiled`. |
| cc19f4bb9 | #5360 | Uses `None` for `attention_metadata` when a layer is missing from the grouped metadata dict, instead of passing the whole dict down (`nnx_decoders.py`, `qwen3.py`, `qwen3_5.py`). |

**Why:** these main changes are relevant to the Qwen3.5-397B MLPerf RL work. They add native FP8 serving and router-quantization control for the MoE/GDN model, fix a vLLM grouped-metadata `AttributeError` on the same path as #5359, and fix AOT compilation of the ragged kernels.

**Notes for reviewers**
- The first three commits applied cleanly. For cc19f4bb9, the source changes applied cleanly, but its test file `tests/unit/grouped_attention_metadata_test.py` doesn't exist on this branch: the branch's port of #5359 (2fd1b5fad) left it out. The commit adds main's current version of that test. See the commit message.
- **Config interaction (edfd9fcc1):** a new check rejects `float32_gate_logits=True` together with `quantize_router_proj=True` when `quantization` is set and `use_qwix_quantization=True`. The Qwen3.5-397B configs set `float32_gate_logits: True`, so enabling qwix quantization with them will now also require `quantize_router_proj: false`. Nothing changes for the current bf16 (unquantized) runs.
- **serve_fp8_weight** is opt-in. It changes nothing unless `quantization: serve_fp8_weight` is set together with an FP8 `weight_dtype`. For RL rollout, the trainer → sampler weight sync would also need to send FP8 weights plus scales. That isn't part of this PR.
- 341466e6e also includes small changes to the shared `dequantize_weight` (handles size-1 scales; leading-dimension scale broadcasting only for weights with ndim ≥ 3). That code path is used even without the new mode.

# Tests

Unit tests on CPU, run from the PR branch with its `src` on `PYTHONPATH`:

```
JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu python -m pytest tests/unit/grouped_attention_metadata_test.py \
  tests/unit/native_fp8_dot_general_test.py tests/unit/quantizations_test.py tests/unit/configs_value_test.py
# 98 passed, 17 skipped

  tests/unit/qwen3_gdn_mamba_slots_test.py tests/unit/vllm_adapter_mamba_block_size_test.py tests/unit/pyconfig_test.py
```

title: Integrate Lineage DeepSeek-V3 model (dsv3.py) into MaxText.
body:
Integrate Lineage DeepSeek-V3 model (dsv3.py) into MaxText.

Adds a `use_lineage` option that runs MaxText's DeepSeek-V3 decoder stack (dense layers followed by MoE layers) through Lineage's `dsv3.dsv3` entry point. All Lineage-specific logic lives in a new Google-internal `experimental/lineage/lineage_adapter.py`, which is excluded from the open-source export; changes to shared MaxText files are limited to wiring.

`experimental/lineage/lineage_adapter.py`:
* Weights: translates MaxText dense/MoE parameter trees into Lineage's `DSv3WeightsPytree` (moving `param_scan_axis` to 0, fusing `wi_0`/`wi_1`) and reshards them to Lineage's layout. Routed experts are sharded `P(None, "expert", "fsdp_moe", None)` / `P(None, "expert", None, "fsdp_moe")` to match MaxText's native `fsdp_moe` placement, removing four step-boundary all-to-all reshards (256 chips: 5,410.3 -> 5,150.0 ms/step synthetic, 7,944.9 -> 7,701.2 ms/step on C4 + `ckpt0424`).
* RoPE: converts the trailing `qk_rope_head_dim` channels of `wq_b` / `wkv_a` from MaxText's interleaved layout to Lineage's split-half layout (`Lineage_yarn(P x) == MaxText_yarn(x)`), closing 62% of the step-0 loss gap (6.585 -> 5.707 nats).
* Segment IDs: reshards `decoder_segment_ids` to match Splash Attention in explicit mode so packed documents stay isolated, closing the remaining loss gap (5.707 -> 5.165 nats).
* Mesh: `build_axis_mapping` derives Lineage's logical axes from `logical_axis_rules`; `create_device_mesh` maps the `['dcn', 'x', 'y', 'z', 'core']` mesh 1:1 onto the physical Ghostfish torus per slice (-2,320.5 ms / -22.6% step time at 256 chips, xid/290538307), falling back to `mesh_utils` otherwise.
* Rounds the capacity factor up to the Pallas GMM tile size and computes a Switch-style MoE load-balance loss from router outputs when `load_balance_loss_weight > 0`.
* Multi-Token Prediction: `fetch_lineage_mtp_weights` / `run_lineage_mtp_layer` run each MTP layer (embedding/hidden-state norms, `eh_proj` and the single MoE layer) through `dsv3_mtp.dsv3_mtp_layer`. Weights use the stack shardings minus the scanned layer axis; activations and segment IDs are batch-sharded over `dcn` + `fsdp_attention`, so MTP works on single- and multi-slice meshes.

MaxText wiring:
* `nnx_decoders.py`: new `elif cfg.use_lineage` branch in the scanned DeepSeek path that calls `lineage_adapter.run_lineage_dsv3` and sows `moe_lb_loss`; `_build_linen_params` also returns the dense `mlp` subtree.
* `multi_token_prediction.py`: `use_lineage` branch in `MultiTokenPredictionLayer` that calls `lineage_adapter.run_lineage_mtp_layer` (`mtp_k_final_norm` stays in MaxText); `_shift_left_one_cp_aware` gathers an explicitly sequence-sharded input before `jnp.roll`, which cannot slice a sharded axis.
* `maxtext_utils.py`: uses `lineage_adapter.create_device_mesh` when `use_lineage=true`.
* `types.py` / `base.yml`: `use_lineage` flag and validation (requires scanned `deepseek` decoder, MLA, YaRN and `capacity_factor > 0`); per-axis parallelism lists are kept as configured for custom physical mesh axes.
* `train.py`: skips the aux-loss-free bias update when no `moe_bias_updates` were produced (the Lineage path does not emit them).
* `deepseek3-671b-lineage.yml`: DeepSeek-V3 671B config on the physical `['dcn', 'x', 'y', 'z', 'core']` mesh.
* `copy.bara.sky`: excludes the adapter, its tests and the lineage config from export.

Lineage:
* `learning/performance/lineage/BUILD`: grants `:dsv3`, `:dsv3_mla`, `:dsv3_mtp`, `:dsv3_types` and `:ops` visibility to the adapter package and MaxText tests.
* `learning/performance/lineage/dsv3_router.py`: wraps the SparseCore-pinned coefficient gather in a `@jax.custom_vjp` (forward `_sc_gather` in logits dtype, backward `_sc_scatter_add_f32` in f32) so XLA's `OffloadGatherToSparseCore` does not fuse an implicit `convert` into `gather_custom_fusion`.
* `learning/performance/lineage/dsv3_sparse_layer.py`: `segment_ids` is a traced array, so it leaves `_dsv3_sparse_layer_vjp`'s `nondiff_argnums` and is carried through the residuals (needed by the single-layer MTP path).
* `scripts/launch_dsv3_batchsplit_maxtext.sh`, `scripts/launch_dsv3_perf_test.sh`: XManager launchers for MaxText + Lineage DSv3 runs. The MaxText launcher defaults to `dataset_type=c4_mlperf` (as in the MaxText DSv3 MLPerf convergence runs); the 256-chip default checkpoint is `ckpt0908`, which includes the per-layer `mtp_k_final_norm`.

Tests: `lineage_adapter_test` (CPU, incl. MTP weights/shardings) and `lineage_adapter_tpu_test` (Ghostfish forward/backward).

Tested:
Unit tests above; 256-chip Ghostfish runs (xid/290319547, xid/290538307, xid/292152200 synthetic, xid/292153498 C4 + `ckpt0424`); 512- and 1,024-chip multi-slice runs (`dan-syn512-0006` 9.64 s/step, `dan-mlpev-1520` reached eval_loss 3.595 <= 3.60 at step 52, `dan-syn1k-1550` 11.38 s/step); 64-chip parity runs (xid/291362265: 363.5 ms vs 371.5 ms pure Lineage; xid/292193282); 256-chip MTP runs (`mtp_num_layers=1`: xid/292594595 synthetic 4.588 s/step, xid/292837352 C4 + `ckpt0424` 7.45 s/step, eval 3.588 at step 59); 64-chip `train_compile` AOT compile with `mtp_num_layers=1`.

title: Add fsdp-as-dp-for-attn-cp-as-ep-for-moe mesh rule and its eval companion
body:
# Description

Adds two custom mesh and rule sets for running DeepSeek-V3 671B at **`per_device_batch_size=0.5`** on **16k TPU v7x chips (32768 devices)**, with eval at **`eval_per_device_batch_size=1/64`**:

- **`fsdp-as-dp-for-attn-cp-as-ep-for-moe`** (train): `fsdp-as-dp-for-attn` plus a `context` axis that the MoE borrows, as in `cp-as-ep`.
- **`fsdp-as-dp-for-attn-cp-as-ep-for-moe-eval`** (eval, via `custom_mesh_and_rule_for_eval`): same mesh and weight rules; only moves `expert` from the batch to the sequence.

## Train rule

| | attention | MoE (between EP all2all) |
|---|---|---|
| `fsdp` / `fsdp_transpose` | DP (attention weights replicated) | FSDP (`embed_moe` / `mlp_moe`) |
| `expert` | DP for activations, FSDP for attention weights | EP |
| `context` | CP (sequence halves), FSDP for attention weights | EP |

- `context` is laid over the **two TensorCores of a chip**. Each chip holds one sequence split in half.
- `exp` → `['context', 'expert']`, so EP = context × expert. `RoutedMoE` now uses the `("context", "expert")` EP axes for both new rules, as it already does for `cp-as-ep`. Without this the MoE would run EP over `expert` only while the weights are sharded on both axes. The -eval rule is normally applied only through `custom_mesh_and_rule_for_eval`, but it maps `exp` the same way, so it is covered in case it is used as the primary rule.
- Attention weights (`q_lora`, `kv_lora`, `embed_attn`) → `['context', 'expert']`. The `context` half of their all-gather stays on-chip. Their gradient needs a reduction over `context` anyway, so sharding them there turns that all-reduce into a reduce-scatter and all-gather, and halves their HBM.
- **`context` is deliberately the last mesh axis.** jax's v7x mesh builder assigns logical axes last-first and offers the core axis first. With `expert` last, a 32-wide expert axis claims `(16, core)` on a 16x16x32 slice, and `context` can then no longer be placed.

## Eval rule

Only the logical rules are swapped at eval (the mesh is built once from the train rule), so `mesh_axes` is identical. Every weight rule is identical too, so the train state is consumed without re-layout. The only change:

- `activation_batch*` / `activation_kv_batch` / `activation_embed_and_logits_batch` drop `expert` → `['data', 'fsdp', 'fsdp_transpose']`
- `activation_length` / `activation_norm_length` / `activation_length_attn` / `activation_q_length` → `['context', 'expert']`

This enables `eval_per_device_batch_size = 1 / (context × expert)`. For 1/64 that means `ici_context_parallelism=2`, `ici_expert_parallelism=32`. The MoE is unchanged: tokens are still sharded over context × expert, which is the EP group.

## Usage (16k chips)

```
per_device_batch_size=0.5 eval_per_device_batch_size=0.015625
custom_mesh_and_rule=fsdp-as-dp-for-attn-cp-as-ep-for-moe
custom_mesh_and_rule_for_eval=fsdp-as-dp-for-attn-cp-as-ep-for-moe-eval
ici_context_parallelism=2 ici_expert_parallelism=32
context_parallel_load_balance=false
eval_sa_block_q=64
# 16 x 4x16x16 slices: ici_fsdp_parallelism=32  allow_split_physical_axes=true
#  2 x 16x16x32 slices: ici_fsdp_parallelism=256 allow_split_physical_axes=false
```

## Things to know

- **`eval_sa_block_q` must be ≤ 64** at 1/64 (4096 / 64 query tokens per device). With 256 the eval compile fails: `q_block_size=256 should divide q_seq_len_per_shard=64`.
- **`expert=32` on 1024-chip slices needs `allow_split_physical_axes=true`**, because 32 is not a product of {4, 16, 16}. `expert` then becomes a 2×16 sub-plane (half of x × y) instead of a single ring. On 16x16x32 slices it maps cleanly onto the 32-long ring.
- **EP=64 doubles ring-of-experts traffic.** With `use_ring_of_experts=true`, each device gathers 64 × 2048 tokens per MoE layer, about 2× the current EP=16 / pdb=1 recipe. All-to-all volume does not grow with EP, so `use_ring_of_experts=false` is worth profiling.
- **Keep `context_parallel_load_balance=false`.** The input pipeline reorders for the train CP size (2) only, while eval splits the sequence 64 ways. The cost is causal imbalance across the core pair during training: the second half does about 3/4 of the attention work.

# Tests

**AOT** of both the train step and the eval step (under `logical_axis_rules_for_eval`) on 32768 tpu7x devices. The config is the DeepSeek-V3 671B MLPerf fp8 recipe (qwix `fp8_full`, ring of experts, tokamax splash/GMM, MTP, custom remat with decoder-input offload) at `per_device_batch_size=0.5`, `eval_per_device_batch_size=1/64`.

| layout | mesh | physical placement | train | eval (1/64) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 × `tpu7x:16x16x32` | data 2, fsdp 256, expert 32, context 2 | expert = z ring of 32, fsdp = x×y, context = cores | 45.0 GB/device | 9.1 GB/device |
| 16 × `tpu7x:4x16x16` | data 16, fsdp 32, expert 32, context 2 | expert = half of x × y, fsdp = half of x × z, context = cores | 55.3 GB/device | 7.4 GB/device |

Global batch: 16384 (train), 512 (eval). Input sharding: `P(('data','fsdp','expert'), 'context')` (train), `P(('data','fsdp'), ('context','expert'))` (eval).

Mesh axes spanned by each collective in the optimized HLO (static op counts, same on both layouts unless noted; DCN collectives lower to megascale send/recv and are not listed):

| | train | eval |
|---|---|---|
| all-gather `context` | 29 (CP key/value gather) | — |
| all-gather `expert+context` | 145 (attention weights, ring-of-experts tokens) | 57 (CP over 64, attention weights, ring-of-experts) |
| all-gather `fsdp` | 109 (MoE / dense weights) | 28 |
| reduce-scatter `context` | 14 | — |
| reduce-scatter `expert+context` | 59 | 6 |
| reduce-scatter `fsdp` | 59 on 4x16x16; 22 on 16x16x32 (XLA all-reduces the rest over the 256-wide fsdp) | — |

No weight re-layout between train and eval, and no gather over `data`.

`train_compile.py` does not compile the eval step. I used a local driver that reuses `train_compile.get_shaped_inputs` / `jit_and_compile` and compiles `train.eval_step` with the eval data sharding under `axis_rules(config.logical_axis_rules_for_eval)`, the same way `train.py` warms up the eval executable. The driver builds the mesh from `get_topology_desc` so that 4x16x16 can be targeted, because `tpu7x-2048` maps to 8x8x16. The AOT used local libtpu 0.0.46, synthetic data and no checkpointing, and dropped `--xla_tpu_rerun_latency_hiding_scheduler_post_sc_assignment`, which crashes the local compiler.

**Sharding dump test**
- New `TEST_CASES` entry in `tests/utils/sharding_dump.py`: `deepseek2-16b`, `tpu7x-8`, 1 slice, fsdp=2 / context=2 / expert=2, ring of experts on. Its golden in `tests/utils/sharding_info/` was dumped by `tests.utils.sharding_dump`. The golden records:
  - attention weights (`query`, `wkv_a`, `wkv_b`, `out`) on `['context', 'expert']`;
  - routed-expert weights on `['context', 'expert']` (expert dim) × `fsdp` (embed);
  - dense, shared-expert and embedding weights on `fsdp`;
  - activations on `P(('fsdp', 'expert'), 'context', None)`.
- **The golden comparison in `tests/unit/sharding_compare_test.py` is restored, on the NNX state.** The NNX-only migration (71d5c4751) removed it along with the Linen driver, so nothing had been checking these goldens since.
  - The test uses the same arguments as `run_sharding_dump` and compares the physical, logical and input (activation) shardings. On mismatch it prints a per-key diff.
  - The other 11 goldens are Linen-era (`.params/['params']/...` keys). Regenerating the existing `cp-as-ep` one gives a ~1100-line diff. The test skips them with a pointer to `run_sharding_dump`, and they are compared again once regenerated. Regenerating them is out of scope here.
- `pytest tests/unit/sharding_compare_test.py` (CPU, TPU plugin): 1 passed, 11 skipped.
- Checked that it catches regressions: changing `kv_lora` to `['expert']` in the rule fails the test with `changed: ...wkv_b...: expected [['context', 'expert'], ...] actual ['expert', ...]`.

**Lint**
- `pre-commit run --files <changed>`: codespell, pylint, pyink, mdformat, yamllint pass.

**Not run:** an end-to-end training workload on 16k chips.

body:
# Description
    
Add support for **Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B** (`model_name=qwen3.8-2.4t-a95b`), a text-only 2.4T-parameter MoE model built on the existing Qwen3.5 hybrid architecture (`decoder_block: qwen3_5`, Gated DeltaNet + gated full attention
  every 4th layer). This PR adds the model config and checkpoint conversion in both directions (HF ⇄ MaxText). It does not change any model or layer code.
    
**Architecture:** 92 layers (69 GDN + 23 full attention), hidden size 8192, 64 query / 4 KV heads with `head_dim` 256, 512 routed experts (top-10) plus 1 shared expert (`moe_mlp_dim` 2048), GDN with 16 key / 128 value heads
  (8:1 ratio), vocab 248320, partial RoPE (0.25, θ=1e7).
    
### Changes
    
 - **Model config:** new `configs/models/qwen3.8-2.4t-a95b.yml`. The name is registered in `ModelName` (`configs/types.py`) and `HF_IDS` (`utils/globals.py`).
 - **HF config** (`hf_model_configs.py`): new `qwen3_8_2_4t_a95b` config (text-only `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), including `bos_token_id`/`eos_token_id` = 248044 to match the reference `config.json`.
- **Parameter mapping and hooks** (`param_mapping.py`): `QWEN3_8_MAXTEXT_TO_HF_PARAM_MAPPING` / `QWEN3_8_MAXTEXT_TO_HF_PARAM_HOOK_FN` reuse the Qwen3.5 implementations. Two small helpers adapt them to the text-only
  checkpoint:
 - `_qwen3_8_wrap_config`: the flat text config is wrapped as `{"text_config": ...}`, the form the Qwen3.5 code expects.
 - `_qwen3_8_rewrite_hf_source`: HF names are rewritten from `model.language_model.*` to `model.*`. This also handles tuple, list and nested destinations.
- **HF shapes** (`hf_shape.py`): `QWEN3_8_HF_WEIGHTS_TO_SHAPE` reuses the Qwen3.5 shape table with the same prefix rewrite. This includes the tuple keys used for GDN QKV/Z and B/A splitting. It is registered in `HF_SHAPE`;
  without it, `to_huggingface` rejects the model.
- **Export generation metadata** (`hf_model_configs.py`, `utils.py`, `to_huggingface.py`):
- The export previously never wrote `generation_config.json`. Qwen3.8 stops on two EOS tokens (`[248046, 248044]`), which `config.json` cannot express, so an exported model loaded with default HF settings would lose EOS
  stopping.
- A new `HF_GENERATION_CONFIGS` table and `get_hf_generation_config()` helper supply the reference generation config per model.
- `save_model_files` takes an optional `generation_config` and saves it next to the tokenizer files, for local, GCS and HF Hub outputs alike. Models without an entry behave exactly as before.
- **Logit checker** (`tests/utils/forward_pass_logit_checker.py`): vision placeholder tokens are now masked only when `use_multimodal=True`. Before, every `qwen3*` model name loaded the Qwen3-Omni multimodal token processor,
  even for text-only models. Text-only prompts contain no vision tokens, so text-only KL results are unchanged.


 # Tests

**Unit tests** (CPU):

 
The new `tests/unit/qwen3_8_conversion_test.py` (18 tests) covers:

- **Setup:** the model is registered in every lookup table (`PARAM_MAPPING`, `HOOK_FNS`, `HF_SHAPE`, `HF_MODEL_CONFIGS`, `HF_IDS`), and every architecture field in the YAML matches the HF config.
- **Parameter mapping:** the `model.*` prefix rewrite and config wrapping; scanned and unscanned mappings (text-only prefix, per-layer attention type, scan-block layer order).
- **Shapes:** every export destination, string **and** tuple, has its own shape entry, and each tuple's shape equals its parts' shapes (138 tuple entries).
- **Hooks, tested on tagged tensors:** the expected layouts are built directly from the architecture, not by calling the hooks. Covered: GDN QKV/Z and B/A grouping at the real 8:1 ratio, the gated full-attention query/gate
split, and expert gate/up split and re-fusion plus `wo`. Each is checked in both directions (HF → MaxText and MaxText → HF).
- **Scanned export:** over two cycles, stacked MaxText tensors are sliced back into per-layer HF tensors via `process_maxtext_param`, and converting HF → MaxText and re-stacking recovers the scanned tensor.
- **Export metadata:** `save_model_files` writes `generation_config.json` (EOS `{248046, 248044}`, BOS/pad 248044) and `config.json` BOS/EOS, verified by reloading with `transformers.GenerationConfig.from_pretrained`.
- **Mutation check:** swapping the V/Z blocks in the GDN hook makes the layout and scanned-export tests fail.

`configs_test.py` now validates `qwen3.8-2.4t-a95b.yml` against the config schema.

# Description

This change resolves an issue with Gemma 4 attention weight initialization and QK normalization:

1. In `src/maxtext/layers/attentions.py`, `init_query_w` now checks `self.use_qk_norm` in addition to `self.config.use_qk_norm`. When `use_qk_norm` is enabled (or `query_pre_attn_scalar != 1.0`), `depth_scaling` is set to 1.0 instead of `sqrt(head_dim)`. This prevents dividing the initial query projection weights by `sqrt(head_dim)`, ensuring unscaled canonical weight initialization for Gemma 4.

title: Add TE Groupe GEMM as GPU GEMM for MoE
body:
# Description

This PR adds Grouped GEMM support to accelerate MoE workloads.
 
At the moment, JAX `ragged_dot` delivers insufficient performance for many MoE scenarios. To address this limitation, an option has been added to execute expert GEMMs using Grouped GEMM instead. Bias support is also fused into the operation, reducing execution time by approximately 20%.
 
## Motivation
 
MoE models use routing, which naturally creates an uneven distribution of tokens across experts. As a result, the number of tokens processed by each expert is dynamic and only becomes known at runtime. This requires a GEMM implementation capable of handling variable workloads for individual experts.
 
In addition, when Expert Parallelism (EP) is greater than one, token buffers must be allocated for the worst-case routing scenario. In practice, this often means that the amount of padding exceeds the number of real tokens.
 
Performing computations over the entire padded buffer results in substantial performance loss. Therefore, a ragged-style execution model is required, where each expert processes only the amount of data actually assigned to it.
 
Grouped GEMM provides an efficient solution to this problem by allowing per-expert workloads with dynamically varying sizes while avoiding unnecessary computation on padding. This significantly improves utilization and overall MoE performance.

title: Fix dropless-replay remat override: match the NNX decoder
body:
The dropless replay program (retry_when_tokens_dropped) is built by reconstructing the model with force_dropless on the MoE modules and remat_policy_override="full" on the decoder, so the worst-case replay recomputes instead of saving activations. The override was applied to modules whose class name is "Decoder", but the decoder class is NNXDecoder, so it never matched and the replay kept the run's remat policy.

With remat_policy=custom and large device-saved tensors this makes the replay program much larger than the training step: on DeepSeek-V3 671B at 1024 chips (EP16 x FSDP128, moe_x_sorted=device) the replay compile needed 253.9 GiB of HLO temporaries (the routed expert input saved at dropless capacity for all 58 layers) and failed, while the training step itself compiles at 42.6 GiB. Matching the decoder by its get_remat_policy attribute lets the override apply; the same replay then compiles at 62.1 GiB, identical to a full-remat replay. The training step is unchanged.

Related: #5348 (moe_x_sorted remat location), which is where this surfaced.
Receipts: AOT compiles on a virtual tpu7x-2048 topology with the team's recipe: replay before 253.89 GiB (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), after 62,125,417,504 B; training step 42,556,076,960 B in both.

title: Adding DualPipe Style Schedule to Improve MoE Performance
body:
# Description

This draft adds an opt-in, layer-level 1F1B gradient-accumulation schedule to MaxText’s normal training entry point. The existing serial schedule remains the default.

With `gradient_accumulation_schedule=dual_pipe`, three microbatches execute as:

```text
F0 → (B0 + F1) → (B1 + F2) → B2
```

Each combined layer-scan iteration contains backward for layer `L-1-k` of the previous microbatch and forward for layer `k` of the next microbatch. Both are inside the same jitted training step, exposing independent work to XLA’s scheduler that could overlap computation and communication.

This is microbatch scheduling within a training step, not distributed pipeline parallelism. It enables overlap opportunities but does not guarantee concurrent execution.

## Implementation

- Adds a JAX scheduler for the initial forward, combined backward/forward scans, and final backward.
- Adds an NNX adapter that reuses MaxText’s existing layers, embedding, and output head, and restores gradients to the original parameter structure.
- Extracts the existing masked loss calculation into a small helper shared by ordinary and dual-pipe training.
- Accumulates gradients with fixed parameters across microbatches and retains valid-token normalization. Optimizer updates remain in the normal training path.
- Handles DeepSeek’s dense prefix and MoE layers as separate homogeneous scan groups.

## Scope and limitations

Initial support covers NNX Llama and DeepSeek with TE-MoE, scanned layers, deterministic execution, and full or no rematerialization. Supported TE quantization recipes are stateless; unsupported configurations are rejected explicitly.

Broader model coverage, custom rematerialization, and mutable layer-state support remain future work. Peak memory can increase because old and next-microbatch residuals may coexist.

This change does not modify TE kernels, weight layouts, or TE-EP bootstrap capacity sizing.


# Tests

The 23 scheduler and NNX-adapter CPU tests pass:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu python -m unittest discover \
  -s tests/unit -p 'dualpipe*_test.py' -v
```

Coverage includes loss/gradient comparisons against reference autodiff, full rematerialization, heterogeneous layer groups, combined BF scan structure, gradient-tree restoration, frozen router state, and TE metric reductions.

The three dedicated shared-loss tests have not run successfully in the local environment because of missing dependencies (`filelock`/`omegaconf`).

The current review branch has not yet been GPU-validated. CPU tests do not establish full-model numerical equivalence, TE communication correctness, or a performance improvement.

## Overview
This PR fixes a critical GDN state corruption and logprob explosion bug in hybrid models (e.g. Qwen 3.5 / Qwen 3-Next) when served via `maxtext_vllm_adapter` with alignment-aware prefix caching enabled (`mamba_cache_mode="align"`).

---

## The Issue 

1. **Metadata Flattening in `adapter.py`**:
   `tpu_runner.py` correctly prepares `GroupedAttentionMetadata` mapping each layer/group to its respective metadata:
   - Groups 0, 1, 2 (Mamba/GDN layers) carry **Mamba block tables** with size proportional to `custom_mamba_cache_multiplier` (e.g., 5 blocks in constrained settings).
   - Group 3 (Full-Attention layers) carries the **Attention block table** (e.g., 14,485 blocks).
   However, `maxtext_vllm_adapter/adapter.py` contained legacy logic that intentionally discarded `GroupedAttentionMetadata` and picked metadata from a full-attention layer (`layer.3`), forwarding only Group 3 to the entire model.

2. **GDN Block Table Indexing Mismatch in `qwen3.py` / `qwen3_5.py`**:
   In `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet`, under alignment-aware prefix caching (`mamba_cache_mode == "align"`), `mamba_state_indices` is `None` and the layer determines state slots via:
   ```python
   block_tables = attention_metadata.block_tables
   write_state_indices = jnp.clip(
       block_tables_sliced[batch_idx, write_col], 0, local_rows - 1
   )
   ```
   Because `attention_metadata` had been replaced with Group 3 (Attention), `block_tables` contained Attention block IDs (e.g., block IDs 14, 28, 42). Since `local_rows = 5`, `jnp.clip` clamped every block ID >= 5 to **slot 4**.
   As concurrent requests generated tokens, they repeatedly overwrote each other's GDN recurrent states in slot 4, causing garbage state retrieval on subsequent turns.

3. **Missing `mamba_cache_mode` in `MambaSpec`**:
   In `adapter.py:patched_get_kv_cache_spec`, `mamba_cache_mode` was not forwarded when creating `MambaSpec`, preventing alignment-aware caching logic from activating in `TPUMambaManager`.

---

title: Fix TE EP capacity sizing for gradient accumulation

# Description

Fix TransformerEngine EP buffer capacity sizing when gradient accumulation is enabled.

Previously, EP bootstrap used the entire accumulated batch to calculate `max_tokens_per_rank`. Each MoE invocation processes only one microbatch, so this unnecessarily increased receive-buffer and staging-buffer capacity with GA, potentially causing OOMs.

This change:
- Divides the loaded batch size by `gradient_accumulation_steps`.
- Preserves sufficient capacity for model initialization and larger evaluation batches.
- Validates GA and FSDP/EP batch divisibility.
- Leaves TE’s receive-capacity calculation and routing headroom unchanged.

For a workload with 6 sequences per GPU and sequence length 4096, the token bound now remains 24,576 tokens/rank regardless of GA.

This addresses EP overprovisioning, not separate XLA buffer-lifetime memory growth.

  - GA=1, 2, 3, 16, and 32.

fix(data): Fail the job on JAX runtime errors from the data iterator
body:
# Description

`loader_exception_guard` now re-raises `jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError` from `next(data_iterator)` instead of turning it into `StopTraining`.

Until now, every exception from the data iterator became `StopTraining`. `train_loop` handles that as a normal finish (`Training stopped: ...`), so Python exits 0. With `colocated_python_data_input=True`, `next(data_iterator)` is a colocated-python call over the IFRT proxy, so a slice failure during that call raises a `JaxRuntimeError` such as `UNAVAILABLE: Connection to IFRT proxy server was terminated`. In a non-elastic Pathways JobSet whose `successPolicy` targets the head, the resulting exit 0 marks the whole JobSet `Completed`. The JobSet is never restarted, and training stops early without an error.

- **Non-elastic runs:** a `JaxRuntimeError` from the data iterator now fails the job, so the JobSet failure policy restarts it.
- **Elastic runs:** no change. `maybe_bubble_elastic_exception()` already re-raises `JaxRuntimeError` when elasticity is enabled. This PR gives non-elastic runs the same behavior for runtime errors.
- **Other exceptions:** no change. `StopIteration` still ends training with "You may have run out of training data", and any other data-pipeline error still becomes `StopTraining`.

A stricter option is to turn only `StopIteration` into `StopTraining` and re-raise everything else. That would change the behavior of every data-pipeline error, so it is left to the data-loader owners.

Context: this was found while investigating b/550371967, a non-elastic Pathways JobSet that did not restart after an interruption. That ticket's main cause is on a feature branch; this issue is separate and is also on `main`.
- In that run, the head's main thread was seen blocked inside this call for more than 60 s (`data_loader.py` `next(self.data_iterator)` → `multihost_dataloading.py` → colocated python). So an interruption can land there.
- This exact failure has not been seen in logs yet.
- The same `StopTraining` → exit 0 → `JobSetCompleted` chain has been seen for checkpoint save errors on the elastic feature branch (run `abhi-20260819-053114`, fixed there in 435377f).

BUGS: b/550371967

# Tests

Unit tests, on CPU:

    PYTHONPATH=src JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu python3 -m pytest tests/unit/data_loader_test.py

- New `test_load_next_batch_propagates_jax_runtime_error`: a `JaxRuntimeError` from the iterator is re-raised. It fails without the `data_loader.py` change.
- New `test_load_next_batch_other_exception_stops_training`: any other error still becomes `StopTraining`.
- `pyink` reports no changes. `pylint` reports only the two existing `unused-argument` warnings at `data_loader.py:91`.

title: guard GDN backward norm on zero tokens and duplicate MoE replay slots
body:
### Summary
Two small numerical stability guards for Qwen3.5-35B / 397B RL training:

1. **Zero-norm backward gradient guard in Gated DeltaNet (`pallas_mosaic_tpu_bwd.py`)**:
   - In `_bwd_gdn_pipeline_body`, `inv_r_q = rsqrt(||q||^2 + 1e-6)` evaluates to `1 / sqrt(1e-6) = 1000.0` on zero/padded tokens (`q_orig == 0`). Because GDN is stateful (`d_q_g = do_h @ state_prev^T` is non-zero from prior active tokens), multiplying by `inv_r_q = 1000.0` at line 331 (`d_q = (d_q_scaled - ...) * inv_r_q`) amplifies gradients on zero tokens by `1000x` per layer.
   - Using the double-`jnp.where` check (`q_is_zero = q_norm_sq == 0.0`) sets `inv_r_q = 0.0` (and `inv_r_k = 0.0`) on zero-norm tokens, cleanly zeroing `d_q` and `d_k`.

2. **Duplicate expert ID guard in MoE Router Replay (`moe.py`)**:
   - `slot_valid` checks `0 <= expert_id < num_experts`, which treats a zero-initialized buffer (`[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]`) as valid and routes all 8 top-k slots of the token into Expert 0.
   - Since genuine top-k routing (`k=8`) always selects distinct experts, checking `has_duplicate` after sorting along `axis=-1` falls back to `auto_indices` whenever duplicate slots are present.

title: Test: XLA:TPU host offload fails inside nested lax.scan
body:
Not for merge. Self-contained reproducer for an XLA:TPU bug, to attach to a report for the compiler team.

A jax.checkpoint policy built with save_and_offload_only_these_names(..., offload_dst="pinned_host") compiles when the checkpointed body sits inside a single lax.scan -- the ordinary scan-over-layers layout of a homogeneous model. Wrapping that scan in a second lax.scan, which is how a heterogeneous layer cycle is scanned (over blocks, each block looping over its own layers), makes the same policy fail with an internal post-optimization error.

The script covers three cases and needs only JAX and a TPU:

  FLAT            one scan over 12 layers                        compiles
  NESTED          scan over 4 blocks x inner scan over 3 layers  fails
  TRIP_COUNT_ONE  scan over 12 layers x inner scan of length 1   fails

TRIP_COUNT_ONE computes exactly what FLAT computes; the only difference is a loop that runs once and produces nothing extra. Both failures are the same symptom the Qwen3-Next block scan hits, down to the shape of the bad bitcast.

This blocks remat offload policies on every hybrid-attention model. The one workaround available to us -- flattening the inner loop into a Python loop so a single scan level remains -- unrolls the block body and costs more HBM than the offload recovers.

title: fp8: drhs_grad_quantization_calibration_method (static range on the weight-gradient arm; removes the per-layer absmax MAX reduction over DCN)
body:
## Summary

Adds `drhs_grad_quantization_calibration_method`: a calibration override for the cotangent of the weight-gradient matmul only (qwix `drhs_grad`, dW = X^T dY) under `quantization=fp8_full`. `null` (default) inherits `bwd_quantization_calibration_method`, so existing configs are unchanged. The activation-gradient arm (dX = dY W^T) keeps its own calibration.

## Why

With `bwd_quantization_calibration_method=absmax`, qwix computes the fp8 scale for each backward matmul as a per-channel absmax over the contracting axis. For the weight-gradient arm that axis is the token axis, which data parallelism shards across FSDP, EP and, in multi-slice runs, across the DCN slices. Every layer therefore carries a MAX all-reduce of the scale vector across slices, and a MAX cannot join the SUM gradient bucket that XLA sinks over DCN. In a two-slice DeepSeek-V3 run this per-layer reduction was the largest remaining DCN cost after the gradient buckets were fixed, and it also carried most of the step-time jitter.

A static range on that arm removes the reduction with no compiler involvement. `fixed,0.01` keeps the loss trajectory identical (to three decimals at every step of a 25-step synthetic run at 2 x 512, and on the MLPerf DeepSeek-V3 recipe with real data, checkpoint restore and eval it reaches the eval target one step earlier than the absmax control). `fixed,0.1` was bracketed and loses a small amount of loss, so 0.01 is the recommended value for this model. The activation-gradient arm must keep absmax: a fixed range on both arms underflows the small dX values through the layer stack.

## Reproducing the two-slice DeepSeek-V3 result (2 x 8x8x8 tpu7x, DCN data parallelism 2)

title: MoE: moe_x_sorted remat location (save the routed expert input; skip the backward dispatch all-gather + ragged sort)
body:
## What

One default-off knob, `moe_x_sorted` (a `RematLocation`, default `remat`), for the ring-of-experts MoE path.

With `moe_x_sorted=device` the routed (expert-sorted) MoE input and its small routing/metadata bundle (sort indices, group sizes, combine weights) are saved across the remat boundary instead of recomputed. The backward then loads the saved sorted input for the up-projection weight gradient rather than re-running `route()`.

## Which communication it saves

Under `remat_policy=custom` the backward otherwise recomputes the whole dispatch: the **EP-axis token all-gather** (the fp8 `moe_quantize_token_all_gather` all-gather over the expert axis, once per token chunk) and the **SparseCore ragged sort** that re-derives the expert order. Both run on the SparseCore collective/offload queue, where they compete with the weight all-gathers and the combine reduce-scatter of the same layer. Saving the sorted input removes both from the backward; the expert GMMs still re-run from the saved tensor. Tags are applied with `jax.tree.map` so a `QArray` input keeps its `qvalue`/`scale` leaves tagged.

## Measured (DeepSeek-V3 671B, 512 chips v7x, EP16 x FSDP64, pdbs 1, seq 4096, fp8_full, `moe_pin_sparse_core_all_gathers=false`)

- Step time 3.484 s -> 3.414 s (-70 ms, -2.0%), mean of steps 10-24; loss trajectory identical (7.989 at step 24 both).
- Profile lanes: exposed SparseCore time 0.63 -> 0.49 s/step; TensorCore lane +68 ms from the extra `mlpwo` recompute (see memory note below).
- Default `remat` reproduces the existing program byte-for-byte (AOT compile identical).

## Memory

Saving the sorted input costs HBM. At the configuration above it does not fit on its own (AOT: 115.7 GB of HLO temporaries vs 94.7 GB available); pairing it with `mlpwo=remat` brings the compile to 76.5 GB and is the measured configuration. Use with a per-device batch small enough for the save, and trade another saved tensor if needed.

## Stacking the fp8 static calibration ranges (#5358) on top: 3.41 -> 3.15 s/step, and the real-data check

The remaining backward cost after this change is the fp8 absmax calibration: per-token abs/max passes over the padded ragged MoE buffers plus a per-layer reduce-max all-reduce for the scale. Two static ranges remove them. `drhs_grad_quantization_calibration_method=fixed,0.01` (the knob added in #5358) covers the weight-gradient arm (dW = X^T dY); the existing flag `bwd_quantization_calibration_method=fixed,0.01` applies the same e5m2 range to the activation-gradient arm (dX = dY W^T). Let's examine the numbers.

Synthetic perf stack of this PR (512 chips, steps 10-24): 3.4137 s/step, then 3.2675 with the dW range (-146 ms: TensorCore -50 ms from the abs/max fusions, exposed SparseCore -92 ms from the reduce-max all-reduce), then 3.1543 with both arms (-113 ms, all VPU). The loss trajectory stays within 0.002 of the absmax control at every step. The earlier both-arms attempt with `fixed,-224,224` diverged, so the range matters; 0.01 is the working setting.

Real data: the MLPerf DeepSeek-V3 recipe on one 8x8x8 slice (c4_mlperf data, checkpoint restore, eval from step 43 toward a target of 3.60; s/step is the mean of steps 10-42, n=33; reference attention settings; MaxText nightly 2026-09-22 plus the #5358 knob; `moe_x_sorted` left at its default here, since the recipe's dropless-retry state copy leaves no HBM for it at 512 chips):

| arm | s/step | eval loss at step 43, and the step at which 3.60 is reached |
|---|---|---|
| ubench recipe (absmax, ragged_buffer_factor 4) | 4.3345 | 3.724, step 50 |
| + dW static range | 4.1692 (-165 ms) | 3.689, step 49 |
| + ragged_buffer_factor 3.5 (control for the next row) | 4.1451 | 3.711, step 50 |
| + `bwd_quantization_calibration_method=fixed,0.01` (both arms) | 3.9839 (-161 ms) | 3.721, step 50 |

Convergence with both arms on three data seeds, target disabled so the runs train through step 59 (eval loss at steps 43 / 50 / 59): seed 1234 3.721 / 3.596 / stopped at target; seed 4321 3.726 / 3.595 / 3.466; seed 777 3.705 / 3.586 / 3.462, all monotone. The unmodified recipe reaches 3.60 at step 50 to 51 on the same seeds. Therefore the static ranges appear to cost nothing in convergence on real data at this scale, and the setting to reproduce is both flags together: `drhs_grad_quantization_calibration_method=fixed,0.01 bwd_quantization_calibration_method=fixed,0.01` on top of the recipe (its `bwd_quantization_calibration_method=absmax` is overridden; pyconfig keeps the last value of a duplicated key). The fallback if a new dataset drifts is the bracket `fixed,0.1`.

## Repro

```
python3 -m maxtext.trainers.pre_train.train src/maxtext/configs/base.yml \
  model_name=deepseek3-671b per_device_batch_size=1.0 max_target_length=4096 \
  ici_fsdp_parallelism=64 ici_expert_parallelism=16 custom_mesh_and_rule=ep-as-dp \
  use_ring_of_experts=true use_ragged_sort=true ragged_buffer_factor=2.0 num_moe_token_chunks=2 \
  sparse_matmul=true megablox=true use_tokamax_gmm=true use_gmm_v2=true use_tokamax_splash=true attention=flash \
  quantization=fp8_full use_qwix_quantization=true moe_quantize_token_all_gather=true \
  weight_quantization_calibration_method=fixed,-224,224 act_quantization_calibration_method=fixed,-224,224 \
  remat_policy=custom qkv_proj=device out_proj=device context=device decoder_layer_input=device \
  moe_pin_sparse_core_all_gathers=false moe_x_sorted=device mlpwo=remat \
  dataset_type=synthetic use_random_routing=true steps=25
```

Related: the same tag was first proposed as part of #4969; this PR carries only the remat-save half, isolated and re-measured on the mlperf6.1-dsv3-v3.0 configuration.

title: Fix pipeline_utils mutating axes_to_remove and add unit tests
body:
# Description

Fixes `remove_gathered_mesh_axes` in `utils/pipeline_utils.py` mutating its `axes_to_remove` argument, and adds the first direct unit tests for `pipeline_utils`.

**The bug.** For every non-MoE leaf, `remove_gathered_mesh_axes` did `axes_to_remove.append("expert")` on the caller's list. `derive_stage_weight_partition_specs` (called from `NNXCircularPipeline.from_repeat_weights_to_bsw`) passes that same list to every leaf, so once any non-MoE leaf has been visited, `"expert"` is also stripped from the routed MoE block (`MoeBlock_0`) of every leaf visited afterwards. That contradicts the docstring ("The 'expert' mesh axis is only retained for the routed block").

**When it shows up.** JAX flattens dicts in sorted key order. In a single decoder layer `MoeBlock_0` sorts before its lowercase siblings (`self_attention`, `mlp`, the norms, `shared_experts`), so it is visited before the list gets polluted, which is why this is easy to miss. With `num_layers_per_pipeline_stage > 1` the stage is an `NNXSequentialPipelineStage` with children `layers_0`, `layers_1`, ...; `layers_0`'s non-MoE leaves are then visited before `layers_1`'s `MoeBlock_0`, and the routed-expert weights of every sub-layer after the first lose their `expert` axis in the BSW partition specs. Reproduction at the `PartitionSpec` level, using a Mixtral-style layer:

```
num_layers_per_pipeline_stage=2
  layers_0 MoeBlock_0/wi_0 -> P('expert', None, 'tensor')
  layers_1 MoeBlock_0/wi_0 -> P(None, None, 'tensor')   # expected P('expert', None, 'tensor')
```

**The fix.** Build a new list (`[*axes_to_remove, "expert"]`) instead of appending to the argument. Results are unchanged for single-layer stages and for non-MoE models; only the multiple-sub-layers-per-stage MoE case changes.

I have only reproduced this at the spec level. I have not run a multi-layer-per-stage MoE pipeline on TPU/GPU, so I can't quantify the runtime effect (I'd expect extra gathering and memory for the expert weights).

**Tests.** `pipeline_utils.py` had no direct unit tests. `tests/unit/pipeline_utils_test.py` (CPU only, `cpu_only` marker) covers:
- the partition-spec helpers (`get_mesh_axis_dim_indices`, `remove_gathered_mesh_axes`, `derive_stage_weight_partition_specs`, `strip_pipeline_repeat_logical_axis`, `is_spec_leaf`), including regression cases for the bug above;
- `is_static_param`, `flatten_nnx_state` / `unflatten_nnx_state`, `advance_rng_state`, the Linen-collection helpers and `PipelineContext`;
- `create_gradient_accumulation_scan`: outputs and gradients (eager and under `jit`) match a plain `jax.lax.scan` over the same step, including the accumulated `bsw` cotangent.

# Tests

```
python -m pytest tests/unit/pipeline_utils_test.py
```

- 44 tests pass on CPU (jax 0.11.1, flax 0.12.9, Python 3.12).
- With only the `pipeline_utils.py` change reverted, 5 failures appear (subtests counted separately): the `non_moe_block` case of `RemoveGatheredMeshAxesTest.test_does_not_modify_axes_to_remove`, `DeriveStageWeightPartitionSpecsTest.test_does_not_modify_axes_to_remove`, the `layers_1` and `layers_2` subtests of `test_moe_block_keeps_expert_axis_in_every_sublayer_of_a_stage`, and `test_moe_result_does_not_depend_on_sibling_traversal_order_sibling_sorts_before`. The rest pass either way.
- `pyink` (indentation 2, line length 122), `pylint` (flags from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) and `codespell` are clean on both files.

title: Support vLLM mamba prefix caching in the Qwen3 GDN layer
body:
## Problem

Under vLLM's mamba prefix caching (`mamba_cache_mode="align"`), a Qwen3.5 rollout on the MaxText-native path dies on the first decode step:

```
File "maxtext/models/qwen3.py", line 913, in __call__
  recurrent_state, conv_state = active_cache.get_gdn_states()
AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'get_gdn_states'
```

`Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` decides whether vLLM is driving paged state by sniffing for one field:

```python
use_paged_state = (
    ... and getattr(attention_metadata, "mamba_state_indices", None) is not None and ...
)
```

But align mode is precisely the mode where tpu-inference stops populating it (`tpu_inference/runner/tpu_runner.py:3220-3246`):

```python
# In align mode (prefix caching), mamba state indices are derived on-device
# from the block tables, so mamba_state_indices is None.
if (self.kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers and getattr(
        self.cache_config, "mamba_cache_mode", "none") != "align"):
    ...  # build mamba_state_indices
else:
    mamba_state_indices = None
```

So `use_paged_state` goes False and the layer falls through to the MaxEngine branch, calling `get_gdn_states()` on the 2-tuple of paged state arrays vLLM handed it.

## Change

Resolve the slots from the mamba block table when `mamba_state_indices` is absent.

Align mode needs the read and write slots to **differ**: a request resumes from the block covering its last already-computed token and writes to the block covering its last token, so a later request hitting that cached prefix can pick up the checkpoint. `run_jax_gdn_attention` already takes `read_state_indices` for exactly this (`tpu_inference/layers/common/gdn_attention.py:50`) — the vLLM path passes it, MaxText did not, so read == write. New `_mamba_block_table_slots` computes both and the call now forwards `read_state_indices=`.

`mamba_block_size` lives on vLLM's `cache_config`, which the layer has no handle on, so the adapter passes it down as a new `gdn_mamba_block_size` config key (0 when not in align mode). `generate_maxtext_config` already does this kind of vLLM→MaxText translation for sharding and MoE padding.

Non-align behaviour is unchanged: the `mamba_state_indices` branch is the same code as before, and `gdn_mamba_block_size` defaults to 0.

## Testing

`tests/unit/qwen3_gdn_mamba_slots_test.py`, 3 passed (CPU backend). Covers the read/write split across a block boundary, clamping into the rank-local range, and per-DP-rank slicing of the block table. The first case is inherently a regression test for the old behaviour — it expects read block 11 and write block 12 for the same request.

title: feat(kda): integrate KDA attention with tokamax backend and CP support
body:
# Description

This PR integrates **KDA (Kimi Delta Attention, a recurrent linear attention mechanism)** into MaxText end to end: the attention layer, the tokamax-backed Pallas TPU kernel, context parallelism (CP), and **decoder wiring via `attention_type='kda'`**. KDA updates its recurrent state with the Delta Rule:

```
S' = S * exp(g_t)
residual = v_t - k_t^T @ S'
S = S' + beta_t * k_t ⊗ residual
o_t = scale * q_t^T @ S
```

The layer follows the Megatron KDA reference and delegates kernel execution to tokamax's Pallas TPU implementation, keeping MaxText free of low-level kernel code.

## Key Changes

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `src/maxtext/layers/attention_kda.py` | New `KimiDeltaAttention` layer and `ShortConvolution`: QKV/beta/gate/output-gate projections, depthwise causal 1D convolution, SiLU activation, always-on QK L2 normalization, per-head RMSNorm + output gate, gate parameters `A_log` / `dt_bias` (matching the Megatron reference); also hosts `halo_exchange_for_conv` for CP |
| `src/maxtext/kernels/kda/` | New `chunk_kda` entry point + tokamax adapter: `[B,T,H,D]` ↔ `[H,B,T,D]` layout translation, lazy import of the KDA API, explicit `mosaic` implementation selection inside `shard_map` |
| `src/maxtext/common/common_types.py` | `AttentionType.KDA` |
| `src/maxtext/configs/types.py` | New `KdaAttention` config (`linear_conv_kernel_dim`, `use_kda_safe_gate`, `kda_lower_bound`, reserved `use_kda_lora`) + validators; `attention_type` Literal gains `"kda"`; `attention_type='kda'` with `scan_layers=true` is rejected at config time |
| `src/maxtext/configs/base.yml` | KDA flags registered; `attention_type` supported list |
| `src/maxtext/layers/nnx_decoders.py` | `NNXDecoderLayer` gains a per-layer `attention_type` override and a KDA branch: builds `KimiDeltaAttention` (no KV cache — recurrent state is carried by the kernel); non-KDA types are untouched |
| `tests/unit/kda_attention_test.py` | Layer/kernel/CP suite (see below) |
| `tests/unit/kda_decoder_integration_test.py` | Decoder-integration suite: config guards + a real-decoder training run |
| `docs/reference/kda_cp_support.md` | Design doc, linked into the Reference toctree |

## Using KDA

Select it like any other attention variant — this mirrors how `attention_type='mla'` is consumed:

```yaml
attention_type: kda
scan_layers: false        # required (KDA layers are not validated in scanned stacks yet)
use_kda_safe_gate: true   # recommended: bounded-decay gate, keeps the recurrence stable
kda_lower_bound: -5.0     # common choice, required in [-5, 0) when the safe gate is on
```

Notes:
- KDA always L2-normalizes Q/K — this is part of the KDA architecture (the Delta-Rule recurrence diverges with unbounded q/k), independent of the shared `use_qk_norm` flag which belongs to dot-product attention.
- `context_parallel_load_balance` is rejected with KDA+CP (token order is load-bearing for the recurrent state).
- KDA has no KV cache; autoregressive decoding is not implemented yet (raises a clear `NotImplementedError`). Train/prefill paths are supported.

## Context Parallelism Support

- The CP mesh axis is taken from `cfg.context_sharding` (default `"context"`; `"expert"` works for expert-as-context) and is threaded consistently through the conv halo exchange, the T-axis partition-spec injection, and `ContextParallelMetadata`
- Under CP without user segments, an all-ones segment tensor is synthesized outside `shard_map` so the kernel can always derive per-rank `cu_seqlens` / chain fields
- `ShortConvolution` pulls `kernel_size-1` left-context tokens from the previous CP rank via `ppermute` inside a dedicated `shard_map`; a clear `ValueError` guards the `kernel_size-1 > T_local` case (multi-rank receptive fields are not implemented)

## Tests and Validation

**Unit tests — 35 TPU tests + 23 CPU tests, all passing** (4×TPU v6e, 2026-09-04):

- Layer/kernel: forward/backward (activations + weights), determinism, padding, packed-segment isolation (cross-row and within-row), precision vs a pure-XLA recurrent reference (FP32/BF16, ULP-based fallback)
- CP: kernel-level equivalence parametrized CP=2/CP=4, CP backward, full-layer CP without segments (dummy synthesis path), **full-layer CP with real packed segments** (segment spanning the rank boundary + boundary exactly at the split; fwd + input/weight grads vs non-CP), oversized-halo rejection, load-balance rejection, CP metadata-missing refusal
- Composition: full-layer **Mosaic vs tokamax XLA reference parity** (same weights, fwd + grads)
- Kernel guards: `initial_state` / `output_final_state` rejected with clear errors
- Markers: `tpu_only` is applied per-test, so the pure config/pure-op tests also run in regular CPU CI

**Decoder integration** (`tests/unit/kda_decoder_integration_test.py`):

- CPU-runnable: config acceptance, `scan_layers` guard, dispatch of `NNXDecoderLayer` to `KimiDeltaAttention` (and unchanged default for other types)
- TPU: a real-decoder training run (`decoder_block=default`, 2 layers, delayed-copy task — i.i.d. tokens with `t[i] = t[i-delay]`, `delay=5` beyond the conv receptive field, so only the recurrent state can solve it; masked loss): **loss collapses from 5.28 to < 1.0 in 400 steps** through the actual decoder

### Reproducing

On a TPU host (Python ≥ 3.12; verified on 4×TPU v6e):

```bash
# 1. TPU-capable JAX (validation used JAX 0.11.0 + libtpu 0.0.44.1)
pip install "jax[tpu]" -f https://storage.googleapis.com/jax-releases/libtpu_releases.html

# 2. MaxText with TPU dependencies
pip install -e <maxtext checkout>
pip install -r <maxtext checkout>/src/dependencies/requirements/generated_requirements/tpu-requirements.txt

# 3. tokamax with the KDA kernels — the KDA API has landed on openxla/tokamax
#    main but no release contains it yet; install from source:
git clone https://github.com/openxla/tokamax.git && pip install -e tokamax
#    (or the equivalent branch validated here: -b antgroup/kda-pallas-kernel, tip 939da5c)

# 4. Tests (kernel/CP tests are tpu_only and skip cleanly elsewhere)
pytest tests/unit/kda_attention_test.py tests/unit/kda_decoder_integration_test.py -v
```

## Dependencies

- The KDA kernels come from [openxla/tokamax#1103](https://github.com/openxla/tokamax/pull/1103) (Kimi Delta Attention Pallas kernels, by @Fred33146). **Status**: the code has landed on openxla/tokamax `main` (signature-compatible with this PR's adapter, verified), but **no public tokamax release contains it yet**. MaxText's pin therefore cannot express the dependency; the adapter imports the KDA API lazily, so installs without it are unaffected until KDA is actually used (clear `ImportError` with instructions at that point). Once the first release ships, the `tokamax>=` pin and derived requirement files will be bumped.
- Validated with JAX 0.11.0 + libtpu 0.0.44.1

## Hardware / Shape Constraints (mosaic kernel)

The adapter selects the `"mosaic"` Pallas implementation explicitly (no silent fallback). Constraints — surfaced as clear `NotImplementedError`s from tokamax at bind time:

- TPU generation ≥ 6 (validated on v6e)
- Key dimension ≤ 256
- Under CP: key and value head dims must be multiples of 128
- Sequence length padded internally to a multiple of chunk size 64

## Known Limitations / Follow-ups

- Autoregressive/inference path not implemented (train/prefill only; AR raises a clear error)
- `initial_state` / `output_final_state` not yet supported (explicit `NotImplementedError`)
- `scan_layers` must be `false` with `attention_type='kda'` (scanned KDA stacks not validated yet)
- bf16 training-recipe tuning for KDA models (the integration test validates in fp32 with the safe gate)
- Hybrid per-layer KDA + softmax models (e.g. Ling-style interleaving) and a production KDA model config
- tokamax version pin bump once the first public release with the KDA API ships

title: fix(qwen3-next): reset GatedDeltaNet state at packed-segment boundaries
body:
## What

`decoder_segment_ids` reached `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` only as `!= 0`, i.e. as a padding mask. When several sequences share a row -- which is what tunix's GRPO packer emits, up to `MAX_SEGMENTS_PER_PACKED_ROW` (16) of them per row in `mlperf_35b_256.sh` -- the delta-rule scan ran straight through the boundaries. Every sequence after the first read the recurrent state left behind by its predecessor, and the depthwise causal conv mixed the predecessor's last tokens into its first `gdn_conv_kernel_dim - 1`.

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B has 30 GatedDeltaNet layers out of 40, and `use_gdn_kernel` is `false` by default, so this is the path the MLPerf run takes.

## How

* `jax_chunk_gated_delta_rule` takes `segment_ids` and restarts the recurrence wherever the id changes. Boundaries are not assumed to be chunk-aligned: tunix's `pack_bin` advances its cursor by the exact sequence length, so they land anywhere inside a chunk. The cumulative decay is measured from each token's own segment start, and every cross-segment pair is masked before the `exp`, so no masked entry becomes `inf` and no difference is taken across a reset.
* `segmented_causal_depthwise_conv1d` evaluates the convolution one tap at a time and drops taps whose source token is in a different segment.
* Padding (id 0) is folded into the sequence that precedes it, so a trailing pad tail does not reset the state prefill hands back to the cache, and the first real token of a left-padded row still receives `initial_state`. Unpacked callers and callers that pass no ids are unchanged.

## Measurements

Four stacked GDN layers, one row holding two packed sequences, comparing the second sequence against the same tokens run alone:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| conv width 4, float32 | 76.7% relative error | 0 (bit-exact) |
| conv width 1, float32 (recurrence only) | 26.4% | 0 |
| conv width 4, bfloat16 | -- | 0 |

The sequence before the boundary matched exactly either way, as causality requires.

Eight sequences of length 17/23/9/41/5/33/28/51 packed into a 256-wide row, so most 64-token chunks hold more than one boundary, each checked against its solo run: worst disagreement 9.2e-5 in float32 and 7.0e-2 in bfloat16, against an output scale of roughly 7.5. That residue is reassociation, not state leakage -- a sequence sits at a different offset within its chunk in the packed and solo layouts, so the chunked matmuls group the same terms differently. Gradients through the packed row were finite.

### Cost

One TPU v5 chip, two GatedDeltaNet layers at the 35B-A3B widths (`gdn_num_key_heads` 16, `gdn_num_value_heads` 32, head dim 128, `base_emb_dim` 4096), bfloat16, `seq_len` 4096 split into 8 segments, forward plus backward under `jit`:

| | median | peak temp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| parent commit | 42.43 ms | 4434.5 MiB |
| this branch | 44.09 ms | 4483.8 MiB |

+3.9% time, +1.1% peak temporary memory, identical HLO flop count. The extra work is the per-tap convolution and the segment masks; the delta rule's matmuls are unchanged. This is a 2-layer microbenchmark on one chip, not an end-to-end step-time measurement.

## Tests

`tests/unit/qwen3_next_vs_reference_test.py::TestQwen3Next::test_gated_delta_net_packed_segment_equivalence` packs three sequences of length 40/37/31 into a 128-wide row -- no boundary chunk-aligned, trailing padding -- and requires each to match its solo run. It fails on the parent commit (`segment at [40, 77) does not match its solo run`, max abs difference 2.86) and passes here.

`tests/unit/qwen3_next_vs_reference_test.py` on CPU: 9 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_qwen3_next_sparse_moe_block`, which also fails on the parent commit.

## What this does and does not establish

This is a correctness fix. Before it, the model computed the wrong function on every packed row in 30 of its 40 layers, and gradients were taken of that wrong function.

It is **not** established that this is the origin of the `grad_norm: nan` in the 35B-A3B GRPO run. No probe produced a NaN from the unpatched GDN path on its own; the observed effect is large numerical error, not a non-finite value. A run of the same recipe from `atwigg/mlperf` HEAD with `--skip_step_on_nan` showed NaN on steps 1, 4, 5 and 6 and clean gradients on 0, 2, 3 and 7 through 13. The packed-segment bleed is present on every step, so it is not sufficient on its own -- a second, batch-dependent ingredient is involved. Whether this branch removes the NaN has to be measured, not inferred; the skip-enabled run gives a rate (4 in 14) to compare against.

## Not covered

* **Context parallelism.** The recurrence keeps its previous behaviour: the ids are withheld at the `shard_map` call site, with a `TODO` there. A shard would have to know whether a boundary falls in a later shard before handing its state on, and `kernels/attention/gdn_cp.py` folds a shard's chunks into a single affine map. The convolution is segment aware on every path including CP, so under CP one of the two leaks is fixed rather than neither.
* **The Pallas kernel path** (`use_gdn_kernel: true`) resets only at chunk-aligned boundaries (`kernels/gdn/gdn_bwd/pallas_mosaic_tpu_bwd.py`), so it is also wrong for unaligned packing. Not touched here. Either the kernel needs arbitrary boundaries or tunix's packer needs to align to `gdn_chunk_size`.

title: fix(vllm): enable Qwen3.5 hybrid GDN paged attention and KV cache spec for vLLM serving
body:
## Summary

Enables Qwen3.5-35B hybrid attention (Gated Delta Net + full self-attention) serving on TPU v6e under vLLM using the MaxText adapter.

Serving command paste: https://paste.googleplex.com/6558303367331840

## Context & Motivation

When attempting to run the Qwen3.5-35B vLLM serving command on `main`, serving fails during model initialization and JIT warmup. While colleagues running experimental branches (e.g., PR #5305 / `wxd/gdn-align-block-table`) had partial workarounds for prefix caching, pristine `main` encounters several blocking issues.

## Issues Addressed & Errors Seen

### 1. Paged GDN State Fallback to MaxEngine Cache
* **Error**:
  ```python
  File "maxtext/models/qwen3.py", line 913, in __call__
    recurrent_state, conv_state = active_cache.get_gdn_states()
  AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'get_gdn_states'
  ```
* **Cause**: In `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet`, `use_paged_state` was gated strictly on `getattr(attention_metadata, "mamba_state_indices", None) is not None`. Under vLLM, `block_tables` is passed instead. When `mamba_state_indices` was `None`, `use_paged_state` evaluated to `False` and incorrectly tried to call `.get_gdn_states()` on the 2-tuple of paged buffers.
* **Fix**: Gated `use_paged_state` on either `mamba_state_indices` or `block_tables` being present. When `mamba_state_indices` is absent, extracted slots from `block_tables[:, 0]` with safe truncation handling.

### 2. Per-Layer Attention Metadata Dictionary Unwrapping
* **Error**:
  ```python
  AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'padded_num_reqs'
  ```
* **Cause**: vLLM passes `attention_metadata` as a per-layer dictionary (`{"layer.0": AttentionMetadata, ...}`). In `qwen3_5.py` and `qwen3.py`, `attention_metadata` was passed as-is to `self.attention(...)`, causing attribute lookups to fail on dictionary objects.
* **Fix**: Unwrapped `layer_attn_md = attention_metadata.get(f"layer.{self.layer_idx}")` if `isinstance(attention_metadata, dict)` in both `Qwen3NextDecoderLayer` and `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer`.

### 3. KV Cache Spec Resolution Timing in vLLM Adapter
* **Cause**: vLLM's `KVCacheManager.get_kv_cache_spec()` is invoked before `runner.model` is instantiated. The existing monkey patch in `adapter.py` checked `if not hasattr(runner, "model"): return original_get_kv_cache_spec(self)`, causing it to fall back to the unpatched spec and allocate standard `AttentionSpec` instead of `MambaSpec` for GDN layers.
* **Fix**: Stored `_maxtext_config` onto `vllm_config` during `MaxTextForCausalLM.__init__` and supported generating or resolving config directly from `runner.vllm_config`. Updated `MambaSpec` uniform page size handling with `dataclasses.replace`.

### 4. Dependency & Import Compatibility
* Added safe fallback imports for `must_fuse_call` in `jax_flash_attention.py` and multimodal utilities in `multimodal.py`.

---

## Operational Note: Memory Headroom
When running `--max-model-len=65536` with hybrid attention, `--gpu-memory-utilization=0.90` left only ~20 MB of free HBM, causing an XLA `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (by 134 MB) during JIT program loading. title: feat(training-engine): optional per-leaf gradient norms
body:
## What

The global gradient norm is one scalar, so a NaN in it says only that some gradient went bad. `log_per_leaf_grad_norm` records the L2 norm of every gradient leaf alongside it, which names the parameter the NaN or Inf came from.

Written while debugging the `grad_norm: nan` at step 8 of the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B MLPerf GRPO run, where the single scalar gave nothing to localise on.

## How

The norms are taken at the same point as the global norm -- after the freeze mask and before clipping. That ordering matters: `clip_by_global_norm` multiplies every parameter by a factor derived from the global norm, so once it has run, one bad leaf has become every leaf and the origin is gone.

Paths are rendered the way `optimizers.get_path_mask_fn` renders them, so a name reported here can be pasted straight into `trainable_parameters_mask`.

Off by default. When on it costs one extra reduction per step, recorded with the rest of the step's metrics, so no extra device sync.

## Known gap

A scanned leaf carries its layer axis, so one norm covers every layer in the block. Marked with a `TODO` in `_per_leaf_grad_norms`.

## Tests

Two added to `tests/post_training/unit/maxtext_engine_test.py`: one checks that a NaN leaf is named and that the rendering agrees with `get_path_mask_fn`, the other that the metric appears only when the flag is set.

`tests/post_training/unit/maxtext_engine_test.py` on CPU: 64 passed, 2 failed. Both failures (`test_gradient_norm_is_recorded_every_step`, `test_maybe_register_pathways_persistence`) also fail on the parent commit.
